newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Opposition opposes bank mergers.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Opposition opposes bank mergers.

text.p: Australian Labor Opposition Treasury Spokesman Gareth Evans said on Tuesday that Labor would oppose the ending of the current so called "six pillars" policy which prevents mergers between four big Australian banks and the two largest life offices.

"We would be opposed to any moves to make it easier for mergers amongst the big six (because) already there was little competition between the existing major players," a Labor spokesman quoted Evans as telling a party meeting.
The spokesman told reporters Evans had said any move to merge those would further reduce what little competition currently existed.
The inquiry into Australia's financial system, established by the government and headed by businessman Stan Wallis, will hand its report to the government by the end of March.
But the public release date of the report has not yet been announced.
The report is expected to include a recommendation to end the current "six pillars" policy.
Analysts also expect it to recommend that mergers be determined by the anti-monopoly authority rather than by a government minister.
